audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 3 and 5 read 'Skill' and row 6 reads 'Yasuo', while the packet chart is Yasuo on rows 0-5 and Vayne on row 6 — and whys[6], spikes[3].text and late all say the two-item mark flips hard to Vayne.
audit.why: The chart rendered a different answer from its own explanation on three of seven rows.
audit.corrected: phases[3]/win[3] and phases[5]/win[5] set to Yasuo, phases[6]/win[6] to Vayne, ratings moved with them.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls Wind Wall's cooldown 'short' and never gives a number, never states that Condemn is a projectile the Wall also eats, never states that Steel Tempest needs two stacks to knock up, and never states that Sweeping Blade cannot be re-cast on the same target.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17s for 4 seconds — calling that short tells you to wait when you should be committing. Condemn carries the projectile flag, so the Wall deletes it. Riot's Q text says the whirlwind only fires at 2 stacks of Gathering Storm, and the E text says it 'Cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds' — both are the concrete spacing cues this matchup needs.
audit.corrected: early, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d rewritten with the duration, the cooldown, the projectile rule and the two-stack rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wind Wall was tracked as the punishable cooldown with no duration or number attached.
audit.why: The 4s up / 25s down split at rank 1 is the whole trading rhythm of this lane.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Wind Wall's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Still his: Wind Wall is 4s of cover on a 19s cooldown by rank 4, and he only needs one knock-up to open the whole trade.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Wind Wall's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King is not enough while Wind Wall answers autos and Condemn alike — wait for item two.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Yasuo carry threat 9/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on: Silver Bolts' true damage shreds his crit build, and Condemn ends the dash-in once the Wall has expired.

edits.before: Yasuo starts ahead: from level 1 he sits behind the wave, and any time you Q in to trade he can E through a minion to punish you or reposition. Wind Wall (available at level 3) negates your autos and your Condemn projectile outright, so respect its short cooldown and don't commit Q into a full wave. Farm safely, take Silver Bolts stacks off him only when the wall is down.
edits.after: Yasuo starts ahead: from level 1 he sits behind the wave, and any time you Q in to trade he can E through a minion to punish you or reposition. Wind Wall lasts 4 seconds and negates your autos and your Condemn projectile outright — but it is 25s at rank 1, so bait it and own the whole gap after. Farm safely, and stack Silver Bolts on him only while the wall is down.

edits.before: Blocks ALL your autos. Bait it, then DPS. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Wind Wall lasts 4s and is 25s at rank 1 — bait it, then commit into the gap.

edits.before: Yasuo wastes Wind Wall — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Sweeping Blade cannot re-dash the same target for a few seconds.

edits.before: That is Yasuo's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: The Wall eats Condemn too — it is a projectile, so never fire E into it.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Steel Tempest only knocks up at two stacks — count them, then step.

notes: The packet itself flags 'level chart contradicts data: Vayne wins 52.68% but the chart gives Yasuo 6/7 stages'. I kept the packet's chart shape because every prose field on the page describes exactly that arc — Yasuo-favoured lane, Vayne-favoured scaling — and a 52.68% edge earned entirely after two items is consistent with it. Raised as a question rather than silently rebalanced. Riot's E text gives no number for the re-dash lockout ('a few seconds'), so no figure was invented.
